title: [Two Pronged] My son’s future wife is 5 months pregnant with someone else’s baby
summary: Our letter sender is worried about her son, who loves someone who came back into his life when she was five months pregnant. How does one respond to a situation like this?

blocks.text: Rappler’s People section runs an advice column by couple Jeremy Baer and clinical psychologist Dr. Margarita Holmes.

Jeremy has a master’s degree in law from Oxford University. A banker of 37 years who worked in three continents, he has been training with Dr. Holmes for the last 10 years as co-lecturer and, occasionally, as co-therapist, especially with clients whose financial concerns intrude into their daily lives.
Together, they have written two books: Love Triangles: Understanding the Macho-Mistress Mentality and Imported Love: Filipino-Foreign Liaisons.
Dear Dr Holmes and Mr Baer,
My son Rafael (29 years old) met his old girlfriend Bea after 12 years of being apart.

Her family left for another country and, being just 17 then, she had to go with them. But she said that now that she has reached the age of majority and can live where she wants, she flew back here because “she could never forget Rafael.”

Rafael was inconsolable when she left. His friends and even his father, encouraged him to meet someone else he could love and introduced him to countless appropriate women. Even when he agreed to go out on dates, his heart was not in it.
We would talk often then. I did my best to console him. He never seemed to get over her.

She, however, seems to have gotten over him, despite her saying she never stopped loving him. She is now five months pregnant. It still doesn’t show, but Rafael told me immediately after she told him.
He plans to marry her as soon as they can. I know they can do it much faster with my support. But I cannot give it.

Imagine, my son being cuckolded like that! I asked him, his friends asked him how he could feel nothing about the fact that he was not her first love. He told them that, as long as he is her last love, he was fine with that.
I told him I could never accept a grandchild that is not of my blood, but he said he was sure I would change my mind after that.
There are other problems surrounding such a marriage. I cannot fathom his even thinking of doing this: a grown man behaving like a 15-year old schoolboy.
Please help,
– Disappointed Mother
Dear Disappointed Mother (DM),
Thank you for your email.
It is entirely appropriate that you should be concerned for your son given the circumstances.
On the face of it, Bea seems to be taking advantage of his feelings for her, having failed (for whatever reason) to marry the biological father of her unborn child.
What is unclear from your account is why Bea has waited so long to return to what she describes as someone she could never forget and never stopped loving.
Her reason for leaving seems valid but surely she could have returned much earlier, once she became legally an adult, if this is truly how she felt/feels.
This is potentially a red flag although of course there may be a perfectly sound explanation which may clear the air.
Having said this and if Raphael insists on marrying Bea, you might perhaps reconsider your opposition to such an outcome.
You say that Bea cuckolded him but this is a gross misinterpretation of the situation.
They were not in any sort of relationship, much less married, when Bea became pregnant and therefore there was no question of infidelity whatsoever.
Her actions may make her protestations of always loving Raphael decidedly questionable but nothing more.

As for your intention to reject her child, are you really going to endanger your relationship with Raphael through such a course of action? You characterize his behavior as that of a 15 year old schoolboy; others might describe it as showing considerable maturity in the face of a full understanding of all the facts.
You supported Raphael when Bea left and during his subsequent 12 years of grief; shouldn’t you be there for him when he then finds happiness with her?
Maybe it’s time to meet with Bea again. You may find a young woman who has more in common with you than you expected; after all, you both love Raphael.
Best wishes,– JAF Baer
Dear DM,

Thank you very much for your letter. I am glad you have mentioned your concerns and your feelings of doubt, and even anger, towards Bea. Not only because she is pregnant with another man’s child, but because you probably feel she did not pine away as deeply, or as intensely, as Rafael did.

True, you are really not clear on what sort of social and love life Bea had the 12 years she was away, but you know enough to presume it was a lot more active than Rafael’s because how else could she have gotten pregnant.

Thus, it seems to me part of your mixed feelings towards Bea is due to what most mothers would feel towards the marriage if they were not comfortable with it: a sense of losing him to his soon-to-be-wife, instead of the old saying that “you are actually gaining a daughter!”
“But what sort of daughter,” you are probably asking yourself, “and even if she answers my questions or ‘volunteers’ some answers, how do I know she is telling the truth?”

Because of the particular circumstances of Rafael’s and Bea’s marriage, it is perfectly understandable for you to feel this way, to be wary of their marriage and yes, even hope it doesn’t pull through. But Rafael seems to dead set on it, as does she, and each will fight any dissension that may come up.

This is probably another reason Rafael’s decisions hurt you so much. You have comforted him as much as you could during his 12 miserable years without her… and then she comes swanning in, without any reasonable explanation except she “could not forget Rafael.”
I can imagine how hard it must be to always hold your tongue and not say to her, “Well, you sure did at least one time 5 months ago.”
How it must have hurt you that you, the only woman in his life for the last 12 years, could be discarded so quickly once the love of his life came back to him.
Dearest DM, I hope you do not think I am making gatong” (making it worse). I am merely repeating what my other clients have told me in similar situations.

You may not see them as “soul mates destined to be with each other for all time,” but Rafael (and, I imagine, even Bea) certainly does. You may not see Rafael as loving her first child as much as he would his future children with her, but again, these soul mates do.

For the sake of your son, and the possible relationship you may have with Bea and her child, I suggest you keep such thoughts to yourself if you are able to. Perhaps this will help make this suggestion more palatable: You cannot be sure your change of attitude (and hopefully the behavior that comes with it) may not necessarily mean all will be okay immediately, especially with you.
BUT you can be sure it will be difficult to repair your growing family, which now includes Bea and her unborn child, if you sully their coming marriage in any way.

This suggestion is not encouraging you to be a hypocrite. Rather, it just encourages you to respond to your resilience over Rafael’s seeming abandonment of you by your acceptance that this is what marriage means in healthy families — your openness to give fate a chance.
All the best— MG Holmes
Life got complicated? Write to our Two Pronged duo at twopronged@rappler.com.
